summary: Security hardening verified end-to-end. Backend: existing test_security.py + test_security_live.py (22 passed) plus new test_security_extra_live.py (17 passed): alg=none / HS256-forged / payload-swapped (sub changed) / tampered cookie / expired (30s token, waited past exp) tokens -> 401 on /api/me, /api/analyses, /api/admin/stats; X-Frame-Options DENY, HSTS, CSP default-src 'none', Permissions-Policy, nosniff present on 200/401/404 responses; /api/openapi.json, /api/docs, /api/redoc, /api/docs/oauth2-redirect -> 404; network limit not bypassed by multi-value X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP, and no new counter docs created by spoofing. Unit (non-live) suite 136 passed. Frontend: Clerk ticket sign-in works, refresh keeps session, Dashboard + all 7 calculators + History load with 200 API calls; member family-pattern public result correct (Boy, 'Stated range: 70-90%' for 3+3, GN-648038FB id, rating + confirmations shown). With this connection's counter set to 60: family-pattern shows localized connection-limit message in data-testid=calculator-error (EN/AR RTL/DE), no result card, 429s; blood-type still 200 with result; admin still gets a result and admin calc does not increment the counter. /admin/stats 'Possible copying attempts' section shows note '20 per account and 60 per internet connection', network blocked = 3 (matches 3 blocked attempts), translated AR (rtl) and DE. Member -> /api/admin/stats 403. Counter restored (count 1, blocked 0), roles restored to member, 3 UI-created analyses deleted (verified 404).

minor.issue: Network limit check-then-increment is not atomic across accounts (_save_locks is per user+kind); concurrent requests from many accounts on one connection can slightly exceed 60. Could use a conditional find_one_and_update({count:{$lt:60}}, $inc) instead.

azp is checked against X-Forwarded-Host/Host header values (every comma-separated entry). Works on preview (browser tokens accepted), but trusting a request header for the audience check is weaker than pinning to a configured app origin env var; consider an explicit allow-list for production.

Responses carry access-control-allow-origin: * (and ingress-level allow-headers *). Acceptable for bearer-token auth with allow_credentials=False, but require_user also accepts the __session cookie; consider restricting CORS_ORIGINS to the app origin in production.
